Read /tmp/claude-501/trail-brief.md and follow it. You are **T6, pipeline observers**. Branch `perf/pipeline-observers`.
Finding: rust-perf #2 (also read #6 for context). The audit says `DurableObserver::record_start` and the other observers run inline on the scheduler task, so a durable start serialises blocking I/O ahead of every dispatch; it was code reading only, never measured. You own `crates/michi-pipeline/src/{observer,exec,record}.rs`-level code and its tests/benches (check what the files are called). **Measure first**: write a test or divan bench with a slow observer and show the scheduler stall (dispatch latency or total time versus observer delay, with several concurrent steps). If the stall is real and material, fix it in the smallest way that keeps the documented guarantee that a start is durably recorded before its effect is dispatched (read `docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md` and `docs/spec/10-pipeline-effects.md` and keep every documented ordering guarantee; do not weaken crash-safety for speed), document the trade-off, and add a scaling/latency regression test that fails on the old behavior. If the cost is not material or the guarantee forbids a fix, make NO code change: write the measurement and the reasoning into `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` and open the PR as docs-only. Say clearly which outcome you reached.

Other trails run at the same time in other worktrees. Edit only files your trail owns. If your change forces a one-line call-site fix in a file another trail owns (for example `napi.rs`), make the minimal fix and say so in your report. Never reformat or reorganize files you do not own. If `git merge origin/main` brings conflicts in your files, resolve them keeping both sides' intent.

Add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` for code changes (look at existing ones and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; package `michi-core` unless your change is elsewhere; start a paragraph with `Breaking:` when behavior or API breaks). No changeset for CI-only or docs-only changes.
